title: xgames-kit play target
description: What a game must play like, as a design a build writes toward and a judge measures against (spec.play.target). Written by the designer round (builder/play/design.mjs) from the person's words, the ledger, the foundation's parts, the references and what the designer knows of the genre; after the look, before the build. Every number is one a judge can measure in real play. It never narrows the idea: what no part does is a build line. It never names a reference game.

from.description: What the designer read beside the person's words: reference frames or clips (refs+words), or the words and genre knowledge alone.

genre.description: The kind of play in plain words ("turn-based artillery", "co-op garden sim"), never a game's name, and what players of such games come for.

verbs.description: The core verbs: what a player does, each on a control.

input.description: The control it is on, in the spec's control words (primary, move, jump …) or keys.

beats.description: The loop's beats: what fills each span of play.

moment.description: What a player does every few seconds (about 5 s).

stretch.description: What happens every half minute or so: a turn, an exchange, a goal taken.

round.description: The whole round, run or match: its arc from start to end.

between.description: Between rounds: what carries over, what makes the next one different.

reach.description: How the objective is reached from where the players start, on this game's own world.

within.description: Seconds a new player takes from a seat to act on the nearest objective (0: it is in front of them).

risks.description: What on this world could make it unreachable (water, cliffs, inside the ground), for the placement and the judge to rule out.

things.description: What the objective places in the world (pickups, zones, goals, targets): each on ground a player can reach.

placed.description: ground: on the world's own ground under it; surface: on top of a prop or structure; zone: an area; carried: on a player; board: a cell of a board; none: not a thing in the world.

reach.description: How a player gets to it: walk (goes to it and takes it: a pickup, a goal, a zone; the default), aim (hits it from where they stand: a target, a rival's character), none (it comes to them). The play judge holds every walk thing to a spot a player can get to.

touchpoints.description: How players affect each other (against or together). Empty only for a game one person plays alone.

pacing.description: The numbers a judge measures in real play (bots and the play-tester).

firstAction.description: Seconds from Play to the first meaningful action a new player takes.

eventsPerMinute.description: Meaningful events (the events marked meaningful) per minute, the whole game.

roundSeconds.description: How long a round, run or match lasts, about.

turnSeconds.description: A turn's length, when players take turns.

idleMax.description: The longest stretch a player may go with nothing meaningful done by or to them (watching another player's turn counts as idle only when nothing on screen concerns them).

comeback.description: The chance a player or side behind at the halfway point still wins (0 when nobody competes).

downMax.description: The longest a knocked player stays down (a tumble, a ragdoll flight, its landing and get-up) before they act again; 0 when nobody is knocked down. Fair play (gate C/D's down rule) takes its limit from it: a chaos game allows long flights, a calm one keeps them short.

out.description: Whether a player can be knocked out of play: never; respawn (out, then back after a while); round (out until the round or match ends, as a sunk worm).

events.description: The gameplay events this game reports by these names (the judge counts them; meaningful ones make eventsPerMinute).

chaos.description: 0 calm and exact … 1 bodies flying, things breaking, surprises every exchange.

comedy.description: Where the laughs come from, when the game is meant to be funny.

juice.description: The feedback that sells an action: shake, hitstop, slow motion, squash, sound, particles.

avoid.description: The failure modes this design must avoid, each with the guard that prevents it.

measure.description: What a judge measures to see the guard hold.

makes.description: What makes it play, in 3–6 lines. Each becomes a promise the play-tester checks (play.<n>).

see.description: What a player sees on their own screen when this holds.

friends.description: Proven only with two player-driven seats.

mechanics.description: The registry's mechanics this design uses, tuned (params), and why. A mechanic the spec has is kept; one added here joins the spec.

build.description: What the build must write new for this play because no part does it. Each joins spec.build (a promise).

what.description: What is built, in plain words (it joins spec.build: the same limits).

how.description: What will be written: rules logic, a module in src/<name>.js, an engine override.

row.description: The ledger line it serves (its id).

params.description: Tuning numbers for rules.params (config/game.json), named in camelCase.

bots.description: How bots play it, so one person still gets the game and a judge's bot run means something.

sketch.description: A card's play in a few words, so the cards of one pitch differ in how they play and the person chooses play, not only look (pitch v2 cards[].play).

style.description: The kind of play: "turn-based artillery", "real-time brawl".

beat.description: What a player does every few seconds.
